events.title: Certiorari Denied in King v. Florida
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the application for a stay of execution and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Michael L. King v. Florida. The application was initially presented to Justice Thomas, who referred it to the full Court. The denial means that the execution of the death sentence will proceed as scheduled, and the Court will not review the case.
events.why_relevant: The denial of certiorari and stay of execution affects the administration of justice and the finality of capital punishment cases.

events.title: Certiorari Granted in Noem v. Doe and Trump v. Miot
events.summary: The Supreme Court granted certiorari before judgment in the consolidated cases of Noem, Secretary of DHS, et al. v. Doe, Dahlia, et al. (25-1083) and Trump, President of U.S., et al. v. Miot, Fritz, E. L., et al. (25-1084). The applications for stay presented to Justice Sotomayor and The Chief Justice were deferred. The cases are consolidated for oral argument, which is scheduled for the second week of the April 2026 session. Briefs on the merits and amicus curiae briefs are to be filed by specified dates in March and April 2026.
events.why_relevant: The Supreme Court's decision to grant certiorari before judgment and consolidate these cases for expedited review indicates their significance and potential impact on legal and governmental processes.

events.title: SCOTUS grants Solicitor General's motion in Pitchford v. Cain
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States granted the motion of the Solicitor General to participate in oral argument as amicus curiae and for divided argument in the case of Pitchford v. Cain, docket number 24-7351. This procedural decision allows the Solicitor General to present arguments alongside the parties involved, potentially influencing the Court's consideration of the case.
events.why_relevant: The participation of the Solicitor General as amicus curiae can impact the Court's deliberations and the outcome of the case.

events.title: Supreme Court releases opinion in Olivier v. City of Brandon (24-993)
events.summary: The Supreme Court released an official slip opinion in Olivier v. City of Brandon. Docket number(s): 24-993.
events.why_relevant: The Supreme Court's official opinion in Olivier v. City of Brandon is a primary legal source. Supreme Court opinions can define binding national law and alter the legal position of the executive branch, federal agencies, states, litigants, and democratic institutions.
